        We're down to the final four in the 2026 WNBA playoffs. The semifinals tip off Sunday as the Dream host the Liberty and the Valkyries take on the Aces. Three of the top four seeds advanced in the first round, with one notable exception, as the eighth-seeded Liberty knocked out the top-seeded Lynx. New York will try to continue its run against the Dream in the best-of-five semis.The Valkyries claimed the final semifinal spot on Friday night, overcoming a 16-point deficit to knock out the Wings. Golden State will now face the reigning champion Aces after Las Vegas took care of Caitlin Clark and the Fever in three games in the first round.The thrilling start to the playoffs is fitting, since the 2026 WNBA season has been groundbreaking, on and off the court. It launched on the heels of a contentious and extended labor battle that resulted in a historic raise for the players (the salary cap increased from $1.5 million in 2025 to $7 million in 2026), and in return, the players raised the bar on a weekly basis. Multiple regular-season records fell this year, from Clark becoming the first player in WNBA history with a 40-point, 10-assist game, to Angel Reese breaking the single-game rebounding record with 26 to Kelsey Mitchell passing A'ja Wilson's single-season points record.Here's how you can follow the playoffs.2026 WNBA playoff bracket

title: Missouri routs Florida: Eli Drinkwitz blasts 'narratives' after first top-10 win as Tigers coach - CBS Sports
description: The Tigers snapped a nine-game losing skid to ranked opponents after Drinkwitz's first win over a top-10 team
body:
The Tigers snapped a nine-game losing skid to ranked opponents after Drinkwitz's first win over a top-10 team
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:45 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz tries to avoid social media as much as possible during the season, but he's always up for a juicy soundbite after a momentum-building victory.Saturday's 45-17 destruction of previously unbeaten and eighth-ranked Florida might've been the best of his career with the Tigers: a four-quarter beatdown of a top-10 opponent, his first such victory at Missouri after 10 losses.It came a week after Drinkwitz watched his team fail to execute down the stretch of a road loss to Mississippi State, another reminder of the SEC's week-to-week gauntlet."Everybody's allowed to get better and improve," Drinkwitz said after his team piled up 560 yards of total offense against the Gators. "After this game, I can't believe anything that y'all write about us or anything on Twitter. After last game, I didn't believe anything that was said about me or our team on Twitter, because none of that matters.
"What really matters is the truth of what your coaches teach you and preach to you and that's what makes a good football team. I know y'all have jobs to do and that's awesome and y'all got to do them, but for us, it's about ignoring the noise and staying focused on our trajectory."
After snapping a nine-game skid against ranked teams, Drinkwitz is now 8-19 against AP Top 25 opponents with the Tigers.Drinkwitz said he "couldn't have cared less" about the "narratives" coming into the game about his program in spotlight games.
"Every game has a life of its own, and it's people searching for crap to talk about," Drinkwitz said.Previously ranked 25th in the AP poll, the Tigers should vault inside the top 20 in Sunday's updated rankings with a winnable home game next week against Texas A&M before facing Ole Miss on the road. Missouri still has to face top-ranked Texas and No. 2 Georgia during the season's second half, creating opportunities for a squad having no issues scoring points this season despite preseason Doak Walker candidate Ahmad Hardy yet to suit up in the backfield.
Ole Miss transfer quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,287 yards and 13 touchdowns without an interception, while running back Jamal Roberts already has three 100-yard games following Saturday's 211-yard explosion against the Gators."Last week (at Mississippi State), we didn't set edges and we didn't tackle ... we didn't have situational execution on third downs in the red zone," Drinkwitz said. "Boom, (we) got them fixed. This week, we better start running the ball better on first or second down or we're going to be in real trouble vs. Texas A&M. "It's constantly figuring out where you got to plug holes. That's our job, and that's what we're going to do."
With four games left against top-10 opponents this season, Drinkwitz can legitimately sell Missouri (4-1) as a potential CFP threat inside his locker room — hopes that can morph into a real expectation if the Tigers win their next two SEC games with the Aggies and Rebels before an open date later this month.

title: Deion Sanders hints at Colorado QB issue after loss to Texas Tech - CBS Sports
description: After a four-interception performance against Texas Tech, the Buffaloes face a three-man open competition under c
body:
After a four-interception performance against Texas Tech, the Buffaloes face a three-man open competition under center as offensive struggles threaten their season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:10 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Colorado has a serious quarterback problem. Deion Sanders won't say it, but he wants everyone else to do just that."You know what it is. If I say it, you're gonna run with it," Sanders said following Colorado's 29-7 loss to Texas Tech. "You know darn well what it is. Just write it yourselves. You know what it is. It's blatant. There's no ifs, ands or buts about it. I would respect y'all a lot more if you just said it yourselves. You know darn well what it is."Despite getting putrid quarterback play on Saturday night, Colorado still led Texas Tech well into the third quarter. Then the Buffaloes threw an interception on three consecutive drives, with two of them coming from quarterback Isaac Wilson. One of Wilson's picks was in the end zone, resulting in a zero-yard pick-six for the Red Raiders.
Wilson finished the game with 290 passing yards, one touchdown and three interceptions. Including a pick thrown by receiver Joseph Williams, Colorado totaled four on the evening.
In his press conference, Sanders insisted upon gesturing toward one position instead of naming it specifically."We got one glaring problem," Sanders said. "Let's stop the shenanigans, man. We got one glaring problem. You guys know darn well what that is. Let's stop the foolishness. We've got to play better at one specific position. That's it."Whether Sanders wants to address the issue himself, quarterback play has severely hindered the Buffaloes. They've yet to score more than 14 points against Power Four competition, and their 394.2 total yards per game rank 14th in the Big 12.
On the whole, Colorado has thrown for just eight touchdowns to six interceptions. That won't get it done, especially in conference play."We've been horrible," Sanders said of the Buffs' offensive struggles. "Don't sugarcoat it. We've been horrible. What'd we have? Seven points. You're not gonna win. Don't sugarcoat it no more. Just tell it how it is."The simple fact is that Colorado has struggled mightily at the quarterback spot since Shedeur Sanders went to the NFL. The Buffaloes started three different quarterbacks last season, and they could be on track to do that again with Kaneal Sweetwyne getting a little action at the end of Saturday night's loss.
It certainly doesn't help matters that Sanders is being intentionally vague about Julian Lewis -- who began the season as Colorado's starter.Sanders tight-lipped about Lewis' benchingWith Lewis faltering in the first four games, Sanders turned the offense over to Wilson against Texas Tech. That wasn't much of a surprise, but the fact that Sweetwyne replaced Wilson against Texas Tech was.In his postgame press conference, Sanders sidestepped a question about Lewis' tumble down the depth chart. In fact, he said he'd prefer Lewis to address it himself.
"I would love for JuJu to come here and he'd tell you what happened," Sanders said. "So, 'You benched JuJu from first to third string.' No, that's not how it went down. It didn't happen like that."Later, Sanders refused to answer a question about Lewis because he didn't play."JuJu didn't play today," Sanders said. "I'm not gonna badger the kid. I'm not gonna say nothing derogatory about the kid. He didn't play today. ... I'm worried about our team and winning. You're trying to single out one kid. You can't do that."Didn't Sanders himself single out Lewis when asked about his benching? Did he not single out the quarterbacks while imploring everyone else to do it for him?
The bizarre echange aside, Lewis is apparently in the mix to start again moving forward with Sanders saying the Buffaloes have "three options" at quarterback as the battle rages on into Week 6."Every darn day is an open competition," Sanders said. "That's the position that is somewhat disabling us and disarming us."

title: UFC 332 fight fallout: Next options for Natalia Silva, Payton Talbott and more - CBS Sports
description: Talbott wants Sean O'Malley, but there might be an even more exciting style clash on the horizon
body:
Talbott wants Sean O'Malley, but there might be an even more exciting style clash on the horizon
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:00 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        SALT LAKE CITY -- Salt Lake City was Knockout City at UFC 332. The card set records for most KOs, most Round 1 KOs and most consecutive Round 1 KOs for a single card in modern UFC history. Many fighters delivered statements that should reward them down the line.The main event was in a difficult position. Natalia Silva and Wang Cong, two fighters known for winning long fights, had to perform for a crowd spoiled with finishes. They showed some fire over 25 minutes, resulting in Silva winning the vacant women's flyweight championship. Her first title defense is obvious. So long as Valentina Shevchenko, who recently vacated the title, plans to return, there will be questions about Silva's reign. But that's not the only option for the new champion.No one is questioning Payton Talbott's potential. The 28-year-old turned in a star-making performance against former two-division UFC champion Deiveson Figueiredo. He now has consecutive wins over former champions in his back pocket and is hunting down a third.
        
            
                UFC 332 results, takeaways: Natalia Silva gets signature moment, major prospects take next step
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
In the aftermath of UFC 332, let's take a look at the best fights to make for the big winners and losers.
Women's flyweightNatalia Silva vs. Valentina Shevchenko or Alexa Grasso 2: Booking the winner's next fight was always simple. Shevchenko never lost the title. She vacated due to injury. The two-time champion has ruled the women's flyweight division with an iron fist for most of its history. If she's healthy soon, she absolutely deserves the next title shot. Grasso is another former champ who deserves a shot. Grasso looks like a new woman ever since losing to Silva. If UFC needs a quick turnaround, I'm sold on this rematch. It'll elevate Silva ahead of an inevitable fight with Shevchenko, or position Grasso to break the 1-1-1 tie she and Shevchenko share. Erin Blanchfield is another option, but I think Grasso has a better claim, even with the recent loss to Silva.Wang Cong vs. Erin Blanchfield or Jasmine Jasudavicius: Wang had moments, but it's evident she wasn't ready for this stage. She'll need a step back in competition. Blanchfield and Jasudavicius fight in Edmonton on Oct. 17. The winner will cover ground in the women's flyweight division. The loser should meet Wang for the opportunity to turn things around.BantamweightPayton Talbott vs. Cory Sandhagen: Talbott called out former UFC bantamweight champion Sean O'Malley after destroying Deiveson Figueiredo. There's nothing inherently wrong with that fight. However, the matchmaking pieces don't fit. If Petr Yan beats Merab Dvalishvili at UFC 333, O'Malley (No. 2) deserves the next title shot. If Dvalishvili wins the title back, it's easier to justify pairing O'Malley with Talbott, who likely takes Figueiredo's No. 9 ranking next week. I'd much rather see Talbott and Sandhagen duke it out. It checks off many of the same boxes as O'Malley-Talbott. Arguably, it's a more compelling striking battle between two of the promotion's most unconventional fighters.
Deiveson Figueiredo vs. Marcus McGhee: Figueiredo looked terrible. Some veterans like King Green, who we'll get to shortly, don't lose their doggedness even as their bodies decline. Then there's Figueiredo, who looked terrified of taking damage after being knocked down 30 seconds into the bout. UFC will want to feed Figueiredo to another rising contender. McGhee scored an impressive first-round KO on Saturday, but it came against a promotional newcomer on three days' notice. Fighting Figueiredo gives more valuable information about McGhee's ceiling.LightweightEsteban Ribovics vs. Renato Moicano or Tom Nolan: Ribovics is ready for the lightweight rankings. He violently dispatched Green, knocking him down three times in short succession. He barely took damage either. Moicano and Nolan headline a UFC Fight Night on Halloween. The winner deserves an upward trajectory. The loser can determine if Ribovics belongs among the lightweight elite. Matchmaking Ribovics is easy because he always produces fireworks. Moicano is cut from a similar cloth.King Green vs. Dan Hooker or Brian Ortega: Green's late-career renaissance comes to an end, as all good things must. Fortunately, he won many fans during fight week. I anticipate UFC will feed Figueiredo to surging young talent, but I'd like them to take a different approach with Green. The lightweight division is packed with aging, fan-favorite action fighters. Two of them, Hooker and Ortega, meet in Qatar on Nov. 21. Pair Green with the losing fighter for a guaranteed barnburner that adds star power to any main card.

title: Why Aaron Boone liked what he saw in Giancarlo Stanton's first at-bat since April despite strikeout - CBS Sports
description: Stanton was called on as a pinch-hitter in the ninth inning of the Yankees' Game 1 loss to the Rays on Saturday
body:
Stanton was called on as a pinch-hitter in the ninth inning of the Yankees' Game 1 loss to the Rays on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:04 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After blowing out the rival Boston Red Sox twice in the Wild Card Series, the New York Yankees were shut down by Tampa Bay Rays ace Drew Rasmussen in Game 1 of the ALDS on Saturday night (TB 1, NY 0). Rasmussen took a no-hitter into the eighth inning before Austin Wells broke it up (by making an out at third). It was the first time New York was one-hit in the postseason. "Every win is an exhale and exciting, and the losses are gut punches," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said after Game 1. "But you've got to just keep moving and know that you're going to have some tough days too." Game 1 marked the return of Giancarlo Stanton to game action. Stanton did not play during the regular season after April 24 due to three separate calf injuries, though he is on the postseason roster as a pinch-hitter. He did not appear during the Wild Card Series. In Game 1 against the Rays, he was sent up to pinch-hit for Ryan McMahon to lead off the ninth inning. The at-bat didn't go well -- Rays closer Bryan Baker struck Stanton out on five pitches -- though it's not hard to see the logic behind the pinch-hit decision. McMahon is a glove-first guy who didn't hit much this year, and Baker has reverse splits. Righties had more success against him than lefties, making the righty-hitting Stanton a better option than the lefty swinging McMahon. 
Even after the layoff, Stanton is a much better bet to tie the game with one swing than McMahon, and if he reached base, 34-steal man José Caballero could pinch-run (Caballero could have pinch-ran for McMahon too, of course). It was a sound pinch-hit decision that just didn't work out. Despite the strikeout, Boone liked what he saw from Stanton during the five-pitch at-bat. "I thought he had a really good at-bat," Boone said. "I thought he was on all (five) pitches.  I thought he was seeing the changeup well.  I thought got a good swing off right out of the bat. I liked what I saw. He took the right at-bat.  He just didn't clip it.  So, yeah, I mean, I'm going to take my shot with a hitter there, and got Cabby to run for him. We'll take our shot right there." Stanton has hit against the high-velocity pitching machine and taken batting practice for weeks as part of his rehab. That isn't the same as hitting in the ninth inning of a 1-0 postseason game, obviously, but Stanton has done as much prep work as possible leading up to his return to game action. In all likelihood, Game 1 won't be his final appearance of the ALDS. 
Now 36, Stanton played 24 games and hit .256/.302/.422 with three home runs before the initial calf injury ended his regular season. He suffered two other calf strains during while rehabbing. They were three separate injuries (two to the right calf and one to the left), not multiple setbacks of the same injury. A year ago Stanton authored a .273/.350/.593 line with 24 home runs in only 77 games around a pair of elbow issues. He has hit 18 home runs in 49 career postseason games, and was named ALCS MVP in 2024. Game 2 of the ALDS is Monday night at Tropicana Field. The Yankees, who are again without star slugger Aaron Judge in this round, will start presumptive AL Cy Young winner Cam Schlittler. The Rays will counter with trade deadline pickup Freddy Peralta.

title: Commanders' Marcus Mariota hurts right knee, ruled out vs. Colts in London - CBS Sports
description: The Commanders are already without Jayden Daniels
body:
The Commanders are already without Jayden Daniels
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:17 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Commanders' quarterback injury woes got even worse Sunday in London: Marcus Mariota, already starting in place of Jayden Daniels (elbow), suffered a right knee injury in the first quarter against the Colts and was officially ruled out. After a short time in the injury tent, Mariota walked back to the locker room for further evaluation.Washington turned to third-string quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis, a seventh-round rookie out of Rutgers, getting his first career NFL snaps.Mariota -- who relieved Daniels in the second half of Week 2 against the Cowboys and started in last week's 33-31 upset win of the Seahawks -- was off to a strong start against the Colts. Washington scored field goals on each of its first two possessions, with Mariota completing three of four passes for 46 yards and also ripping off a 35-yard run. But he went down on a red-zone sack, with his right leg getting pinned awkwardly. He was able to walk off under his own power, albeit gingerly.
Kaliakmanis was the 223rd overall pick in April's draft and won the Commanders' third-string quarterback job with a strong preseason.
The Commanders do not have a fourth quarterback on the roster behind Daniels, Mariota and Kaliakmanis; Sam Hartman is on the practice squad. Colson Yankoff, a tight end who started his collegiate career as a quarterback, would be the emergency option.

body:
The two best-of-five semifinal series begin on Sunday ... so who will be moving on to the 2026 WNBA Finals?
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 4, 2026

    10:22 am ET

            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The semifinals of the 2026 WNBA playoffs have arrived. Only four teams remain alive in the hunt for this season's championship, and they'll all be in action on Sunday when the semis start with a doubleheader featuring the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces against the Golden State Valkyries. The Atlanta Dream follow versus the No. 8 seed New York Liberty, who pulled off a major upset to be here. The rest of the best-of-five semifinals will follow the same pattern, with doubleheaders followed by off-days. Game 2 of both series will take place on Wednesday, with both Game 3s on Friday. If necessary, the Game 4s will be on Oct. 11, followed by Game 5s on Oct. 14. Here is a closer look at Sunday's schedule:No. 8 New York Liberty at No. 4 Atlanta Dream, 2 p.m. ET -- ABC/fuboNo. 3 Las Vegas Aces at No. 2 Golden State Valkyries, 4 p.m. ET -- ABC/fuboBefore the semifinals begin, here are the teams our experts expect to advance:
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 Atlanta Dream vs. No. 8 New York Liberty
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Lindsay Gibbs

    Gibbs: Liberty in 5Watching the Liberty in the first-round series against the Minnesota Lynx, I felt the same way I feel when I wipe the smudge off my glasses: oh right, *this* is what things are supposed to look like! For essentially the first time, the Liberty have looked like the championship contenders they were at the start of the season. Now, Atlanta is a much harder matchup for New York than Minnesota was, because the Dream have a lot of size and athleticism. The Dream won the season series 2-1 over the Liberty, with the final two games being fairly easy Atlanta wins to close out the regular season. But I'm hesitant to look too much into those -- in the second one, Breanna Stewart sat out and the Dream had much more to play for.
The X-factor for this series will be Leonie Fiebich. She had one point combined in those back-to-back losses to the Dream. She is going to need to hit a couple of 3-pointers a game to open things up for New York. This is going to be a really physical, fun series, but the Liberty have the best player on the court in Breanna Stewart and the championship experience to come through in the clutch.Maloney: Liberty in 4I picked the Liberty to win the title before the season, and against the Lynx, they finally looked like they could actually do it. Maybe they'll make me look like a sucker for believing in them again, but I can't help it. I'm back in. They've always had the talent, even without Satou Sabally, and the championship experience; against the Lynx, they had a newfound level of focus and cohesion. The Liberty won't be able to bully the Dream, but they're still the biggest team in the league and seemed willing to lean into that advantage in the first round. If they can match the Dream's level of physicality and aggression and make this matchup about skill, they have much more of that on the offensive end. The Dream shot 33.7% on jumpers this season, the worst mark of any playoff team, and among playoff teams, their 0.925 points per possession in the halfcourt was better only than the Valkyries. 
Plus, I just don't want to pick against a healthy Breanna Stewart again. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Golden State Valkyries vs. No. 3 Las Vegas Aces
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Lindsay Gibbs
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Jack Maloney
                            
            GSV vs. LV
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Aces
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Aces
                    
    
    Gibbs: Aces in 4I picked against the Aces in the first round, but I didn't feel great about it. So now, despite the fact that I still have concerns heading into the semifinals -- notably their lack of depth, in particular the absence of NaLyssa Smith -- I can't bring myself to pick against them for a second straight series.It won't be an easy series, though. The Valkyries faced a lot more adversity against the Wings than I expected, but I actually think that will help them in the semifinals. They had to dig deep, withstand streaky scorers, make adjustments and figure out a way to win when they weren't playing their best. Golden State lost all three of its regular-season matchups against the Aces, but notably, all three games occurred in May and June, so well before Smith was out for the season. The Valkyries have grown since then.But the thing about the Aces? They have A'ja Wilson. In the first round against the Fever, Wilson averaged 32 points, 11.7 rebounds, 1.7 steals and 2 blocks per game, shooting 64.6% from the field and 66.7% from 3-point range. That is comically incredible basketball. The Valkyries will get one of the first two games at Ballhalla, but the Aces will win it in four to get back to the Finals for the fifth time in the last seven years, and we will be treated to another showdown of Wilson and Stewart in their primes. Sign me up.
Maloney: Aces in 4Neither of these teams was particularly convincing in the first round. The Valkyries needed a miraculous second-half comeback in Game 3 of their matchup with the Wings, while the Aces nearly blew a double-digit lead in the second half of their own Game 3 against the Fever. This was the semifinal matchup I expected when I filled out my bracket before the playoffs, and at that time, I had the Aces. Nothing I saw in the first round convinced me to change my mind. The Valkyries' defense can hit heights no other team can match, but their offensive swings are far too wild, as we saw in Game 3. Regularly going on extended scoring droughts is not a recipe for success against an Aces team with A'ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chlesa Gray, three of the most consistent offensive players in the league. 
And as great as the Valkyries' defense is, their thin frontcourt has no answer for Wilson, who did whatever she wanted in the regular-season series, which the Aces won, 3-0. The Vakyries' heavy 3-point rate always gives them a chance, but I'm not betting against the Aces' core and their championship mettle.

These moves certainly affect the 2026-27 Fantasy basketball rankings and have ramifications on when to target these players in Fantasy basketball drafts. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown are both in Philly, Kawhi Leonard is back in Toronto, Giannis Antetokounmpo headed to Miami, and Ja Morant is in Portland. Top picks AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer should have the opportunities to produce right away. These first-year players are often the most difficult to project, so having the right 2026-27 Fantasy basketball advice is crucial. This model is powered by the same people who powered projections for all three major Fantasy sites. These cheat sheets and rankings, available for leagues on many major sites, are updated multiple times every day. Last year the model called a sleeper season for Kevin Porter Jr., predicting he would perform much better than his ADP of 70, which was 30th amongst guards. The result: Porter was one of seven players to average at least 17 points, 7 assists and 5 rebounds as he finished 16th among guards in Fantasy points per game. The model also nailed Jordan Poole as a bust last year as he averaged his fewest points, rebounds and assists in five seasons and called Paolo Banchero's and Victor Wembanyama's breakout seasons before they went on to win NBA Rookie of the Year honors as well.Now, SportsLine has simulated the entire NBA season 10,000 times and released its latest Fantasy basketball rankings 2026-27, along with plenty of sleepers, breakouts and busts. Head to SportsLine now to see these 2026-27 Fantasy basketball rankings.   Top 2026 Fantasy basketball sleepersOne of the top 2026 Fantasy basketball sleepers the model is predicting: Lakers center Walker Kessler. The former Jazz big man landed a 4-year, $130 million contract with Los Angeles to be the third cog of their new Big Three behind Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. Kessler fell off the radar last year due to playing just five games because of season-ending shoulder surgery, but he should provide value on both ends of the court and is the ideal center to pair alongside Doncic.Mavs centers Dereck Lively and Daniel Gafford put up their best numbers by rim running and catching lobs from Doncic, which is a skill that Kessler also brings. But neither of those Dallas centers had the defensive presence of Kessler, whose 2.4 blocks per game are second most among all active players, trailing only Victor Wembanyama. He also ranked fifth in rebounds (12.2) in his last full season and shoots nearly 70% from the field. Kessler is the No. 13 center in the 2026 Fantasy basketball rankings, on par with the likes of Kristaps Porzingis and Rudy Gobert. See more Fantasy basketball sleepers 2026 here. He averaged 23.5 points, 6.4 assists and 3.1 rebounds while knocking down 44% of his 3-point attempts.With the retirement of Russell Westbrook and the departure of DeMar DeRozan, Acuff has very little in his way in terms of opportunities with the Kings. He should be a focal point of Sacramento's offense, which gives him the chance to pile up lots of stats. The model likes him above several more established guards such as Trae Young, Jalen Williams and De'Aaron Fox. Identify other Fantasy basketball breakouts 2026 here. Top 2026 Fantasy basketball busts As for players to avoid, the model lists Nets forward Julius Randle as a Fantasy basketball bust. A three-time All-Star, Randle was shipped from Minnesota to Brooklyn, where he's part of a franchise in the midst of a rebuild. Randle is the only player on the team over 30 years old, and it's a team that has seven first-round draftees over the last two years alone. Add in that Randle has a player option for 2027-28 -- meaning this upcoming year is essentially a contract season -- and he's projected to be phased out while younger players get more opportunities.Randle did have a solid scoring season a year ago with the Timberwolves in averaging 21.1 points, but his rebounds dipped to a career low of 6.7. He ranked 12th in total minutes played, but it's hard to see him approaching anywhere near that court time this year, considering no Nets player ranked in the top 90 in minutes played last season. After being a top 15 Fantasy forward last season, SportsLine's model has Randle outside the top 20 at the forward position this year. Avoid these 2026 Fantasy basketball busts as well.
